@ an event read at sample, or with no clock, is its last value up to the frame, 0 before the first event
@ an event read at sample / 4 is the value before the frame of each tick, kept four frames, in a let and inline: the event of a tick frame is seen at the next tick
@ a computed expression of an event read at sample is the last value of the expression, and at sample / 4 the value it had at the tick, in a let and inline
@ d * r is computed at each event with the r of that call and kept; (d at sample) * r is computed at each frame with the r of the frame
process 0 params r=10 frames=6 in x=[2 3 4 6 5 8]
process 0 params r=100 frames=2 in x=[10 7]
process 1 params r=10 frames=6 in x=[2 3 4 6 5 8]
process 1 params r=100 frames=2 in x=[10 7]
@ prev~ and delay~ of an event give the event one and two before, read at sample as the last output
@ the output of prev~ and of a call with no name in an expression of sample is the last output of the event
@ m.vel and vel(m) are the vel of the last event, 0 before the first one; the whole read first has vel 100 (Msg.default()) before it
@ an element of a tuple that is an event is the element of the last event
@ sample_tick() -% last, with last the time kept at the on events, is 0 at an on event: the expression of the event is always 0 when every event is on
@ the difference to the time kept is a value of the event (computed at the events and kept); the elapsed time is with (last at sample)
@ an event read as a name in each copy of a par is the last value
@ an event given to a flow input of sample is read as the last value
@ TBL[d % 4] and mix(d, 7) are expressions of the event: 0 before the first event, not the table or the function of 0; with (d at sample) or x the expression is computed at sample
@ a delay of the event stored where it is written above the maker and through ^ below it give the last value of the frame, one frame later
@ a run cut in calls anywhere (in a grid, with a call of 0 frames) has the values of one call: the last event and the value kept at the tick are in the state
@ reset puts the last event and the value kept back: no event, the grid from its first tick, 0
